title: Announcing the Expo App Awards 2026 winners
summary: Meet the winners of the Expo App Awards 2026, picked from 1,487 submissions, plus every nominee across all five categories.
body_markdown:
This year, 1,487 apps were submitted to the Expo App Awards. To every team and solo developer who entered: thank you!


Going through all the apps and debating the winners is one of my favorite activities at Expo. To be clear, it’s an excruciating process. And you all made it particularly difficult this year. But holding all your clever apps in our hands and scrolling, clicking, flipping through them is a reminder of why Expo exists in the first place.


The mission here has always been (and will always be) to help people get their ideas to users. It was a pleasure to see all your ideas come to life.


Today we're celebrating the winners in all five categories, plus the nominees who made the shortlist. We were supposed to livestream the winners today but a critical mass of the attendees were unable to make it so we’ll reschedule the stream and announce winners here on the blog.


Without further ado…


## Most Innovative Winner: TrainAR


[TrainAR](https://apps.apple.com/app/trainar/id6786016889) is an AI training platform for the trades (gas, heating, plumbing and electrical) in the UK. An experienced engineer wears AI glasses on real jobs so the AI can learn the steps, tools and safety checks, then it guides an apprentice live by voice on the same kind of job and checks each step before they move on.


The phone app is the hub: one Expo codebase for iOS and Android that pairs with the glasses over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, streams the glasses camera and mic in real time, and keeps working on sites with no signal thanks to on-device job packs and on-device speech.


It doesn’t take a product genius to see the myriad ways that this technology could be applied across dozens of industries. Which is exciting. The other thing we loved about this concept is how it’s leveraging technology to *create more jobs* for people.


Truth be told this was the most difficult category to judge because a lot of the innovative app concepts requried access to the tools that accompany the app. For example,[Neko Health](https://www.nekohealth.com/us/en) has an innovative body scan technology that serves data to their app. We didn’t have access to that. And[Bird Buddy](https://www.mybirdbuddy.com/) looked awesome but we didn’t have the birdhouse camera that connects to the app.


My point is that we saw a ton of innovative ideas and the actual testing of them was the challenge. I have some ideas for how to address this categoty differently next year.


## Community's Choice Winner: Supernova


Community's Choice is the one award we don't pick. You do. After community votes on[X](https://x.com/expo/status/2124890615381155966?a=WKZuzVJQ86bWr54zG5E&s=20) and[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7530643791049854976) , the winner is[Supernova](https://apps.apple.com/app/supernova-ai-spoken-english/id6447939054) .


We actually know this team pretty well because we interviewed them for[a case study](https://expo.dev/blog/supernova-ios-keyboard-extension-expo) a couple months ago.


Supernova is an AI English tutor for learners in India, with more than 26 million downloads. Most learners are working professionals who practice spoken English with an AI tutor for job interviews, promotions and everyday conversations at work, and get feedback on pronunciation and fluency in their own language. Supernova is the first app in the team's Expo monorepo, where shared packages handle login, payments, onboarding experiments, push notifications and over-the-air updates.


It’s a fun, creative, and deeply satisfying UI. The onboarding experience feels personal - there is a character that actually talks you through it. We all found that to be very charming. We’re glad you did too!


Supernova's team, five developers in Bangalore, runs three apps from that codebase, including Superflow, a voice keyboard that turns speech in your mother tongue into polished English. None of them had written native iOS or Android code before Superflow, so agents wrote the first drafts of its native keyboard and widget, and tests on every pull request plus telemetry from real phones caught what the agents missed. Agents also check their own work: with agent-device, an agent drives the simulator, taps through each change and takes screenshots. Read the full story in[the Supernova team's post on the Expo blog](https://expo.dev/blog/supernova-ios-keyboard-extension-expo) .


## Most Creative Winner: Doodle Brawl


[Doodle Brawl: Ink Hero](https://apps.apple.com/app/doodle-brawl-ink-hero/id6815540477) is a side-scrolling beat 'em up set in the margins of a school notebook. You play a red-pen stick hero fighting the Eraser King across 100 stages, and there are no sprites at all: the ruled paper, pencil hatching, ink splashes and handwritten fonts are all drawn in code as live ink strokes on a single Skia canvas, in 15 languages.


The game is[built by a solo developer in Korea](https://www.linkedin.com/in/youngmin-lee-06055aab/) . It’s one Expo codebase for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android.


The art direction is why it won “Most Creative”. Every stroke of the game is beautiful and unique - from the notebook paper to the Eraser King. It’s all drawn live in code instead of shipped as sprites.


A handful of us have become pretty hooked on it.


## Largest Scale Winner: Rips by Triumph


[Rips by Triumph](https://apps.apple.com/app/rips-by-triumph/id6751921248) lets collectors open digital packs of real, authenticated and insured trading cards, then keep, ship or sell back every card they pull. Since launching in October 2025, Rips has grown to 5.9 million registered users.


In July 2026 the team rebuilt Rips on Expo SDK 57, and the new app took over the live App Store listing. It uses nearly 40 Expo packages alongside the team's own Expo Modules in Swift and Kotlin, and Expo Workflows build a development client with a QR code for every pull request so reviewers can try changes on a real phone.


I’ll never forget the first time I saw this app. It was shortly after that July rebuild. We were at an Expo offsite and there was a crowd of like 10 Expo developers all huddled around[Joe Ryan](https://x.com/joe_d_ryan) watching him rip Pokemon packs in the app. There was a lot of shouting and celebrating. It’s a memorable app experience. Executed at substantial scale.


It won Largest Scale for serving 5.9 million registered users, and for moving an app of that size onto a rebuilt Expo SDK 57 codebase that took over its live App Store listing.


## App of the Year Winner: Chime®


[Chime®](https://apps.apple.com/app/chime-mobile-banking/id836215269) is our App of the Year, for keeping app quality high across hundreds of screens used by more than 10 million monthly active members. We had the pleasure of speaking with Mark Goldstein, Staff Engineer at Chime, about how the team does it. To him, it starts with **dogfooding** .


> *"At Chime, we have a strong dogfooding culture. Employees across the company use the latest pre-release build of our app every day as we make changes. With so much of the company on it, we get an early read before anything reaches our members."*


Chime uses over-the-air updates to get changes onto employees' phones within seconds, so dogfooding keeps pace with development.


To deliver a best-in-class app, Chime pairs that with a design system that carries a lot of the visual consistency. On top of that, every screen reports the same performance and stability telemetry, like load time and errors. That way, each release rolls out with good observability.


Delivering an app to more than 10 million members changes how you think about and measure quality. In Mark's words:


> *"Every percent matters. If something affects 0.1% of members, at our scale, that's over 10,000 people. Reliable telemetry and alerting are essential to keeping the experience stable for our members."*


Scale also raises the stakes on every release. That's where Chime's member obsession pays off. Dogfooding catches problems before a release goes out, and telemetry spots them during rollout, so teams can fix issues before more members run into them.


For more on how the team works with agents, watch Mark's Chain React 2026 talk,[Your agents can run, now what?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yXtnaBM-zFE)


Congratulations to the whole Chime team. You should all be proud of this app.


Chime is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services are provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. or Stride Bank, N.A.


## Honorable mentions


Making the shortlist out of 1,487 submissions is an achievement in itself. Congratulations to every nominee. Each of these apps had plenty of arguments for being a winner. We hope you submit again next year and we’ll be in touch to learn more about your projects.


**Most Innovative:**[Orbits](https://apps.apple.com/app/orbits-your-home-handled/id6751995632) ,[Kilo](https://apps.apple.com/app/kilo-code-code-with-ai-agents/id6761193135) ,[Hunting Game](https://apps.apple.com/app/hunting-game-irl-manhunt/id6471968553) ,[FlightCatcherPro](https://apps.apple.com/app/flightcatcherpro-plane-spot/id6749510087) and[Neko Health](https://apps.apple.com/app/neko-health/id6751233363) .


**Community's Choice:**[Take Take Take](https://apps.apple.com/app/take-take-take-chess/id6754937311) and[Matiks](https://apps.apple.com/app/matiks-brain-games-puzzles/id6738620563) .


**Most Creative:**[Doodraw](https://apps.apple.com/app/doodraw-animated-drawing/id6758965666) ,[Stompers](https://apps.apple.com/app/stompers-walking-step-counter/id6477849675) ,[Lawa](https://apps.apple.com/app/lawa-step-challenge/id6745783333) ,[Customuse](https://apps.apple.com/app/customuse-ai-3d-creator/id1606479305) and[Mekuru](https://apps.apple.com/app/mekuru/id6792955764) .


**Largest Scale:**[Jack in the Box](https://apps.apple.com/app/jack-in-the-box-order-app/id1283768751) ,[Unidays](https://apps.apple.com/app/unidays-student-discount-app/id599608562) ,[Ryt Bank](https://apps.apple.com/my/app/ryt-bank-ai-powered-bank/id6480042570) ,[Jerry](https://apps.apple.com/app/jerry-save-time-and-money/id1258315950) and[Shotgun](https://apps.apple.com/app/shotgun-live-music-experience/id760028892) .


**App of the Year:**[Superfan](https://apps.apple.com/app/superfan-social-music/id6443763704) ,[Wellspoken](https://apps.apple.com/app/wellspoken-articulation-coach/id6752822613) ,[Runway](https://apps.apple.com/app/runway-ai-image-video/id1665024375) ,[INTVL](https://apps.apple.com/app/intvl/id6472631698) and[WeWard](https://apps.apple.com/app/weward-the-walking-app/id1454213029) .


## Thank you


Thank you to everyone who submitted, voted, shared the polls and tuned in. Every one of the 1,487 apps is proof of what this community can build, and we can't wait to see what you ship next.
